title: Private Equity Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay with a 38-Hour Week
description: Understand how to convert a private equity salary or any hourly rate to annual pay using a 38-hour week, 52-week year. Includes tax, super, and award rate comparisons.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, 52-week year, annual gross pay equals hourly rate × 38 × 52.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries or occupations and are often higher. Most employees are covered by an award, which also includes penalty rates, allowances, and overtime. Check the relevant pay guide at for your industry.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee is currently 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your pay. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830, meaning super is only paid on earnings up to that amount. For example, if your annual salary is $100,000, your employer contributes an extra $12,000 to your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the 38-Hour Week

In Australia, full-time work is commonly based on a 38-hour week. This standard comes from the National Employment Standards and is used by the Fair Work Ombudsman for calculating minimum wages and award rates. When you see a **private equity salary** quoted as an annual figure, it is almost always built on this 38-hour foundation. Converting that annual number back to an hourly rate helps you compare it with award rates or casual work.

## From Hourly to Annual: The Formula

The basic conversion is straightforward:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a 38-hour week, this becomes:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $50, your annual gross pay would be $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It is a useful starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

If you are evaluating a **private equity salary** that is quoted as $200,000, you can reverse the calculation to find the implied hourly rate: $200,000 ÷ (38 × 52) ≈ $101.21 per hour. This helps you see whether the role includes expectations of long hours or weekend work that might not be captured in the annual figure.

## The Fortnight View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the same $50 per hour example:

- Weekly pay: $50 × 38 = $1,900
- Fortnightly pay: $1,900 × 2 = $3,800

Understanding your fortnightly amount is helpful for budgeting and comparing with pay cycles. Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your hourly rate and see both weekly and fortnightly figures instantly.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or occupation. Awards also include penalty rates for evening, weekend, and public holiday work, as well as allowances for specific tasks.

You can find the correct award for your job using the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. These guides list the minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates for each classification. If you are comparing a **private equity salary** with an award-covered role, remember that the award rate is the floor—your salary should be at least that amount when broken down hourly.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For example, the casual rate under the National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using our [the timesheet](/) tool, you can check a box to add the 25% casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading—the tool adds it for you.

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross pay. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 for 2026–27. So if your annual salary is $120,000, your employer contributes an extra $14,400 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit. For more details, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Income above that is taxed at progressive rates:

- $18,201 to $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 to $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 to $190,000: 37%
- Over $190,000: 45%

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The single reduction thresholds used here are based on 2025–26 figures, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this estimate. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to see your net income after tax and Medicare.

## Private Equity Salary in Context

A **private equity salary** often appears as a high annual figure, but it is important to understand what it represents. Does it include superannuation? Is it based on a 38-hour week or longer hours? Are there bonus components? By converting the annual figure to an hourly rate using the 38-hour week formula, you can compare it with other roles, including those covered by awards. For example, the ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time was $2083.70 per week in May 2026, which equates to an hourly rate of about $54.83 for a 38-hour week. A **private equity salary** of $200,000 implies an hourly rate of around $101, well above the average, but you should also consider the total hours expected.

Remember that this conversion is an estimate. It assumes consistent hours, no unpaid overtime, and no salary sacrifice. For a more detailed breakdown, refer to our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide and the [reference tables](/data) for tax and super rates.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
